title: Introduce RippleAttn cascade kernel and steady KV batcher
author: Lena Ortiz
description: Context: We need an alternative attention execution path that improves mid-sequence throughput for mixed-length workloads without regressing tail latency for short requests. This PR introduces 'RippleAttn', a cascade-style attention kernel that composes a fast single-pass QK reduction with an opportunistic secondary pass for fused rotary/rope transforms. It also adds a lightweight KV 'steady' batcher that maintains warm KV slots and performs gentle eviction to stabilize the cache hit-rate under bursty traffic. Motivation: Existing fast-path kernels excel for uniform long sequences but suffer when the workload mixes short and long sequences and when KV cache churn is high. Delta goals: +5-12% p99 throughput on typical customer chat traces, +8% average token throughput for mixed workloads, no >5% regression on sub-64-token tail latency. Design summary: - RippleAttn cascade kernel: two-stage pipeline where stage-1 performs QK matmul with attention scores using a fused FP16 accumulation path; stage-2 runs rotary/rope adjustments and softmax in a compact fused microkernel only for lanes where numeric adjustments are necessary (e.g. large rotary offsets or quantized buckets). This reduces work for short sequences and preserves numerical fidelity for long sequences. The kernel auto-selects based on sequence-length histogram hints passed by the scheduler. - Steady KV batcher: a background batching loop that groups KV reads by hot-slot, issues continuous-batcher-style fetches, and maintains per-shard warm counters. Eviction is 'steady' (rate-limited LRU with tenant-aware demotion) to avoid cascade evictions during bursts. - Scheduler hooks: new hints (seq_histogram, hot_slot_candidates) are surfaced in the request router; the planner uses these hints to steer requests to RippleAttn-compatible workers or fall back to the standard kernel. The change includes runtime feature flags to toggle the new path per-deployment. Checklist: - [x] RippleAttn kernel implementation (CUDA + CPU fallback) - [x] Steady KV batcher implementation and config knobs - [x] Scheduler integration and routing hints - [x] End-to-end unit + integration tests - [x] Microbench harness and perf regression tests - [x] Documentation draft (internal ops runbook) Related: ENG-4032 (attn-kernel roadmap), ENG-4088 (kv-cache stabilization). This description contains implementation rationale, benchmark summary, and operational notes.

release_notes: Introduce RippleAttn cascade kernel and Steady KV Batcher behind runtime feature flags. Expected throughput gains on mixed-length workloads; configurable via router.hints and per-deployment flags. See internal runbook for rollout and rollback steps.
notes: Rollout plan: enable on a small canary fleet with :ripple flag, monitor p95/p99, KV hit-rates, and hot-slot evictions. If eviction rate > 0.5% in 10m window, automatically revert using runtime flag. Ops runbook included in docs/internal/ripple_ops_runbook.md. Perf numbers are from bench/attn/ripple_bench.py using real chat histograms anonymized from customer traces.
safety_considerations: No user-visible API changes. Feature gated and disabled by default in hosted. KV eviction policy is tenant-aware; added guardrails to avoid noisy-neighbor impact.
